Chapter 9: The Ongoing Work of Forgiveness
Forgiveness—let’s be honest, it’s one of the toughest things to actually live out, even for people who talk about it all the time. Most of us carry scars, don’t we? Some are still raw, others have been festering for years. And deciding to truly let go of resentment... it’s never a simple switch you can just flip.
Forgiveness is a journey. It’s not a once-and-done deal.
Picture someone replaying an old hurt—the kind of memory where the words still sting, even after all these years. It’s so tempting to hold onto that, to keep tending the wound, sometimes even waiting for an apology that might never come. But here’s something important: unforgiveness comes with a price. It seeps quietly into our relationships, into our health, even into how we see ourselves.
Imagine this: after years of silence, a letter shows up. The words are simple, but suddenly, there’s a door open that wasn’t there before. Now, there’s a choice—do you keep holding onto the pain, or do you take that first, shaky step toward healing? It’s rarely a straight path. Most days, it feels like you’re making progress, only to slip back again. But with each real moment of forgiveness, the burden gets a little lighter.
What a lot of people don’t realize is that forgiveness is a gift we give ourselves just as much as to the other person. It’s about setting ourselves free, making room for something new to grow inside. Sure, the road is bumpy. There are setbacks—moments when anger flares up, times when that old pain sneaks back in. But with time, resentment’s grip starts to loosen.
For many, faith becomes the anchor for this whole process. It’s the belief that grace is possible—even when it feels like no one deserves it. And here’s the thing: forgiveness isn’t a finish line. It’s ongoing. There will always be more to release, more to let go. But every single act of forgiveness brings a little more freedom, a little more peace.
You start to realize that forgiveness isn’t about forgetting, or pretending the hurt never happened. It’s about making a conscious choice to move forward—to let the past stop controlling your future.
The journey is long, sure. But the peace you find along the way? That’s absolutely worth it.
